items.title: Brownian Motion
items.code:
import numpy as np

def simulate_brownian(T=1.0, N=1000, paths=5):
    dt = T / N
    dW = np.random.normal(0, np.sqrt(dt), (paths, N))
    W = np.cumsum(dW, axis=1)
    W = np.hstack([np.zeros((paths, 1)), W])
    return W

# Properties: W(0)=0, independent increments,
# W(t)-W(s) ~ N(0, t-s)

items.title: Ito's Lemma
items.code:
# If dX = mu*dt + sigma*dW
# and f(X,t) is twice-differentiable:
#
# df = (df/dt + mu*df/dX + 0.5*sigma^2*d2f/dX2)*dt
#      + sigma*df/dX * dW
#
# Key example: f(X) = X^2
# d(X^2) = (2*mu*X + sigma^2)*dt + 2*sigma*X*dW
#
# The 0.5*sigma^2*d2f/dX2 term is the Ito correction

items.title: Geometric Brownian Motion
items.code:
import numpy as np

def simulate_gbm(S0, mu, sigma, T=1.0, N=252, paths=10000):
    dt = T / N
    Z = np.random.standard_normal((paths, N))
    increments = (mu - 0.5*sigma**2)*dt + sigma*np.sqrt(dt)*Z
    log_returns = np.cumsum(increments, axis=1)
    S = S0 * np.exp(np.hstack([np.zeros((paths, 1)), log_returns]))
    return S

# dS = mu*S*dt + sigma*S*dW
# Solution: S(t) = S(0)*exp((mu-sigma^2/2)*t + sigma*W(t))

items.title: Black-Scholes PDE
items.code:
# PDE: dV/dt + 0.5*sigma^2*S^2*d2V/dS2 + r*S*dV/dS - r*V = 0
#
# Boundary conditions:
#   Call: V(S,T) = max(S-K, 0), V(0,t)=0, V->S as S->inf
#   Put:  V(S,T) = max(K-S, 0), V(0,t)=K*exp(-r*(T-t))
#
# Risk-neutral pricing:
#   V(S,t) = exp(-r*(T-t)) * E_Q[max(S(T)-K, 0)]
# where Q is the risk-neutral measure

items.title: Greeks Formulas
items.code:
from scipy.stats import norm
import numpy as np

def greeks(S, K, T, r, sigma):
    d1 = (np.log(S/K) + (r+sigma**2/2)*T) / (sigma*np.sqrt(T))
    d2 = d1 - sigma*np.sqrt(T)
    return {
        'delta': norm.cdf(d1),                      # dV/dS
        'gamma': norm.pdf(d1)/(S*sigma*np.sqrt(T)),  # d2V/dS2
        'theta': -(S*norm.pdf(d1)*sigma)/(2*np.sqrt(T)) - r*K*np.exp(-r*T)*norm.cdf(d2),
        'vega':  S*np.sqrt(T)*norm.pdf(d1),          # dV/dsigma
        'rho':   K*T*np.exp(-r*T)*norm.cdf(d2)       # dV/dr
    }

items.title: Monte Carlo
items.code:
import numpy as np

def mc_option_price(S0, K, T, r, sigma, paths=100000, option='call'):
    Z = np.random.standard_normal(paths)
    ST = S0 * np.exp((r - 0.5*sigma**2)*T + sigma*np.sqrt(T)*Z)
    
    if option == 'call':
        payoffs = np.maximum(ST - K, 0)
    else:
        payoffs = np.maximum(K - ST, 0)
    
    price = np.exp(-r*T) * np.mean(payoffs)
    se = np.exp(-r*T) * np.std(payoffs) / np.sqrt(paths)
    return price, se  # price + standard error

items.title: Options Payoff
Put-Call Parity
items.code:
# C - P = S - K*exp(-r*T)
# Rearranged: C + K*exp(-r*T) = P + S
#
# If violated, arbitrage exists:
#   If C - P > S - K*exp(-r*T):
#     Sell call, buy put, buy stock, borrow K*exp(-r*T)
#   If C - P < S - K*exp(-r*T):
#     Buy call, sell put, short stock, lend K*exp(-r*T)
#
# European options only (American may violate)

items.title: Black-Scholes
Greeks Table
items.code:
# Greek    | Measures        | Call    | Put
# ---------|-----------------|---------|--------
# Delta    | dV/dS           | +       | -
# Gamma    | d2V/dS2         | +       | +
# Theta    | dV/dt (decay)   | -       | -
# Vega     | dV/d(vol)       | +       | +
# Rho      | dV/d(rate)      | +       | -
#
# Delta-hedged portfolio: hold -delta shares
# Gamma scalping: profit from rehedging as S moves
